name: three-stage
title: Three.js stage
description: The shared runtime of the photographic three.js items (vinyl-scrubber, safe-vault): a scene drawn into an OffscreenCanvas in a module worker, or on the page where a worker can't draw, started once input has been quiet after the controls paint, paused off screen, dropped back to the item's drawing when WebGL is missing or its context is lost, and paced for software GL. Also a dark softbox studio environment through PMREM, staged texture uploads and seeded canvas textures.
docs: `createThreeStage(host, { slot, worker, runner, state, onSize, onRenderer })` adds a canvas with `data-slot={slot}` to `host` and gives `host` `data-renderer="webgl"` after the first frame. `worker` starts the item's module worker, written as `() => new Worker(new URL("./x-worker.js", import.meta.url), { type: "module" })` in the item's own file so the bundler builds it; `runner` loads the same runner for the page. `state(view)` returns what to draw, with `view.inView` and `view.reducedMotion`; call `refresh()` when it changes, and `asset(name, canvas)` to hand the scene a picture drawn on the page. In the worker, `serveStageRunner(factory)` answers the page, and `createStageRunner(canvas, size, events, scene factory, initial state)` draws a `StageScene` once per change and every frame only while `animating(state)`; on a software renderer it waits 150 ms for changes to settle and draws at most 15 frames a second at 0.75 device pixels. `three-studio` holds `studioEnvironment(renderer, softboxes, cubeSize)`, `prepareScene`, `disposeAll`, `isSoftwareRenderer` and `stagePixelRatio`; `three-textures` holds `canvasTexture`, `repeating`, `noise` and `seededRandom`.
